5: Unit 2 reads the rules the code holds.
Microsoft Learn's application management policies A P I overview describes two kinds of policy.
The tenant default policy always exists, is disabled by default, and holds separate restrictions for application objects and for service principal objects.
The program sets the same restrictions on both.
An app management policy is assigned to one app, and an app takes only one.
It overrides the default for the restrictions it defines, and anything it doesn't define falls back to the default.
The program's design guidance uses it for an exception: documented, time-limited, with a record number and an end date.
Neither kind blocks tokens for an existing app; only the create or update that breaks the policy is refused.
